To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MDR1 mRNA is expressed at a low level in CLL, and the expression is independent of clinical stage, time of disease, absolute lymphocyte counts, and prior treatment.
the level of MDR 11 gene expression in CLL is generally lower than that in normal lymphocytes and that this level of expression is not associated with the clinical stage of the disease.

the level of mRNA expression for the multiple drug-resistant gene is high in chronic lymphocytica leukemia (CLL) and that this expression is independent of clinical stage, time since diagnosis, absolute lymphocytic count, and lymphocyte surface markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new and more sensitive techniques for measuring the expression of the multidrug resistance (MDR) gene in chronic lymphoid leukemias (CLL) in order to determine the role this gene plays in these leukemias.
the development of a rapid, nonradioactive method for quantifying mRNA levels of a target gene in a clinical sample.
the role of the multiple drug-resis tance (MDR) genes and the P-gly coprotein in chronic lymphocyt leukaemia (CLL).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MDR1-gene is expressed in the majority of CLL-patients, and that this expression is not related to any of the parameters studied in the present study.

the MDR 2 gene is expressed in the majority of cases of CLL, that this expression is not related to the clinical course of the disease, and that the P-glyco protein, the product of the MDR gene, is not expressed in the majority (if not all) of CLL cells, at least as judged by immunocytochemical staining.
the level of MDR1 mRNA in CLL is generally very low and is not related to any of the factors studied.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDR 2 gene is expressed in CLL and that the level of MDR 2 mRNA in CLL is generally lower than the level in normal peripheral blood mononuclear cells.
the MDR  gene is not a major determinant for the resistance of CLL to chemotherapy.
MDR 1 expression is not a general phenomenon in CLL, and the expression of P-glycoproteins is low or undetectible in these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MDR  1 gene is expressed in CLL cells, and this may contribute to their resistance to chemotherapy, as has been suggested for other hematological malignancies.
the level of MDR  1 gene expression in CLL is low, and that this may be a reason why the cells are not resistant to chemotherapy in vivo.
the MDR  1 gene is expressed at low levels in the majority of patients with CLL, and that the level of MDR1 gene expression does not correlate with any of the factors analyzed.
